title: People Are Getting Off to Porn About ICE Raids
gist: A niche but growing pro-MAGA porn scene has taken root on X, fusing white-nationalist rhetoric, AI-generated imagery, and kink subcultures (gooning, financial domination), enabled by the platform's post-2022 moderation shift and monetized through funnels to OnlyFans; scholars read it as fascist sexual politics finding a new distribution layer.

insights.claim: X's shift to a more laissez-faire moderation policy after its 2022 ownership change, which also made the platform a hub for conservative and right-wing commentary, created the permissive environment in which pro-MAGA porn accounts could take root and grow.
insights.speaker: Jason Parham
insights.so_what: Moderation policy changes at a major platform can create downstream space for extreme fringe content categories that wouldn't have scaled under stricter enforcement.
insights.quote: After ownership changes in 2022, X embraced a more laissez-faire approach to moderation, becoming a hub for conservative and right-wing commentators.

insights.claim: WIRED identified about a dozen X accounts producing pro-MAGA porn content, some with tens of thousands of followers, indicating the subculture has moved beyond a fringe curiosity into an audience of meaningful scale.
insights.speaker: Jason Parham
insights.so_what: A double-digit count of accounts with five-figure followings signals an emergent, trackable content category rather than an isolated anomaly.
insights.locator: WIRED identified a dozen accounts, varying in reach

insights.claim: An editor of a widely shared gooner-content page on X reports that MAGA porn accounts, which used to have negligible followings, now have much larger audiences and actively solicit him to feature their material, showing the subculture is reaching for mainstream adult-content distribution channels.
insights.speaker: Jason Parham
insights.so_what: Cross-promotion requests from MAGA-porn creators to larger adjacent content curators show the subculture actively seeking wider distribution, a leading indicator of further normalization/spread.
insights.quote: You’d see [these pages] once upon a time, and they were irrelevant. They’d have like 10 followers. Now they have much bigger audiences.
insights.locator: One editor of a gooner music video page

insights.claim: Pro-MAGA porn spreads in part by overlapping with established niche adult subcultures such as gooning and financial domination (findom), borrowing their existing audiences and distribution networks rather than building reach from scratch.
insights.speaker: Jason Parham
insights.so_what: Fringe political content can piggyback on the existing infrastructure and audiences of unrelated kink communities to accelerate its reach.

insights.claim: At least one account, @MagaGodJ, pairs white-nationalist and homophobic text with what appear to be AI-generated images of idealized bodybuilders, showing generative AI imagery being used as a low-effort content-creation tool for this political-fetish niche.
insights.speaker: Jason Parham
insights.so_what: Generative image tools lower the production barrier for extremist-themed adult content, letting accounts scale output without real models or footage.

insights.claim: OnlyFans creator MasterJoe produces explicitly MAGA-coded dominance content (a submissive wearing a 'Harris-Walz 24' shirt being taunted and mocked) and uses X posts as a promotional funnel to sell a paid video, demonstrating a direct commercial pipeline from free political-fetish content on X to paid OnlyFans sales.
insights.speaker: Jason Parham
insights.so_what: X functions as an unpaid marketing channel that converts political-fetish attention into paid OnlyFans transactions, an underappreciated monetization pathway for platform-adjacent adult commerce.

insights.speaker: Jason Parham
insights.so_what: If fandom self-reports view the content as persuasive rather than purely titillating, political-fetish media may function as an informal, unmeasured political-messaging channel outside traditional campaign or ad-disclosure frameworks.

insights.claim: Rutgers scholar Whitney Strub argues that fascist sexual politics inherently trend toward sadomasochistic dynamics of dominance and submission, tying the current pro-MAGA porn wave to older white-nationalist tropes like the Great Replacement theory.
insights.speaker: Jason Parham
insights.so_what: An academic framework linking authoritarian political ideology to sadomasochistic sexual expression gives platforms and researchers a lens for anticipating similar content clusters around other far-right movements.
insights.quote: Fascist sexual politics tend toward the sadomasochistic—the dominance of the master race combined with the submissiveness to the authoritarian.

insights.claim: Strub situates today's MAGA sex accounts as a continuation of earlier internet irony and meme subcultures, specifically Something Awful, 4chan, and groyper meme culture, suggesting the same online lineages that produced alt-right meme politics are now producing alt-right pornography.
insights.speaker: Jason Parham
insights.so_what: Tracing a direct lineage from ironic meme forums to explicit political-fetish content suggests platforms should treat this not as a new phenomenon but as the latest stage of a known radicalization-adjacent content pipeline.
insights.quote: These MAGA sex accounts strike me as the next stage of those trajectories, filtered through the ironypilled sensibilities of Something Awful, 4chan, and groyper meme culture.

insights.claim: The White House, the Department of Homeland Security, and X all declined to respond to WIRED's requests for comment, and the account @MagaGodJ blocked WIRED's reporting account after being contacted, illustrating a pattern of institutional and platform silence around this content category.
insights.speaker: Jason Parham
insights.so_what: Uniform non-response from government agencies and the platform itself signals no active accountability or moderation posture toward this content, leaving it to grow unchecked.

insights.claim: Beyond pro-Trump political messaging, several of the same accounts also post content normalizing incest, misogyny, and rape themes, indicating the political-fetish niche overlaps with, and may serve as a gateway to, more broadly extreme adult content categories.
insights.speaker: Jason Parham
insights.so_what: The same accounts driving political-fetish content also traffic in other extreme, moderation-flagged content categories, suggesting a single enforcement gap covers multiple harm vectors at once.
